Its forthcoming game in the Mass Effect sci-fi series has been cancelled, and more than 400 people are losing their jobs. As someone who has worked in the video games industry for 15 years and spent almost 20 as a BioWare fan, I am among millions of mourners today. It’s not terribly hard to see why BioWare got the chop. items.title: Bitcoin hovers near $80,000 and Ethereum at $2,370 as macro uncertainty and weak institutional flows weigh on crypto markets
items.excerpt: In recent developments, Bitcoin has dropped to roughly $80,685, while Ethereum hovers around $2,370 due to various market influences. Major altcoins such as XRP and Dogecoin have also experienced dips, some decreasing by 2.2%. A noticeable decline in institutional interest is evident, with substantial outflows from Bitcoin and Ether ETFs. Both Bitcoin and Ethereum are facing challenges sustaining their momentum amidst the market's volatility.

items.title: Lenskart, Meesho among top picks as value retail leads India's consumption story: Siddhartha Khemka
items.excerpt: Value-focused retail formats are growing, while premium categories experience challenges due to stock availability issues. Recent demand fluctuated with a dip noted in September and October, with expectations for improvement in mid-October. Beauty products significantly influence sales, contributing to the overall trends in the market. Rural incomes may pose risks to discretionary spending as festive season approaches. Companies with effective inventory management and store-level traction are better positioned for growth.

items.title: How to win the investing game? Charles Ellis says make fewer mistakes, focus on long-term goals
items.excerpt: Ellis compares investing with tennis to explain why many investors struggle to outperform the market. In amateur tennis, the winner is often the player who makes fewer unforced errors rather than the one who produces spectacular shots.

items.title: Jio IPO GMP today: Grey market signals over 22% listing gains; check allotment, listing date
items.excerpt: The issue, which closed for subscription on October 23, received an overwhelming response from investors, with the overall subscription reaching 22.19 times the shares on offer. The offering has also become India’s largest-ever IPO, surpassing Hyundai Motor India’s Rs 27,870-crore issue in 2024.

items.title: Jio IPO breaks multiple records: From fundraising to investor demand, how the mega issue rewrote India’s IPO history
items.excerpt: The issue set records across fundraising, anchor investor demand and applications, while attracting the highest qualified institutional buyer (QIB) subscription among India’s five largest IPOs. It was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of opening and received nearly 1.4 crore applications, according to figures compiled for the issue.

items.title: Sebi orders Avadhut Sathe, academy to refund Rs 546 crore
items.excerpt: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has directed Avadhut Sathe Trading Academy to refund ₹546.18 crore to investors. Avadhut Sathe and his academy provided unregistered investment advisory services under the pretext of education. The regulator found that misleading testimonials were circulated while concealing overall trading losses. A penalty of ₹11.5 crore was imposed on Sathe and the academy for their actions.

items.title: Anthropic IPO: What should investors consider when valuing the AI company? Aswath Damodaran explains
items.excerpt: Anthropic is on track for an IPO expected in mid-November, reporting impressive revenues of $16.3 billion. However, the company faces a staggering net loss of over $80 billion for the year. Valuation expert Aswath Damodaran warns that IPO investor metrics can be erratic and heavily influenced by market sentiment. As Anthropic navigates an evolving business model, investors are advised to look beyond venture capital evaluations for a clearer understanding.

items.title: Growth, value stocks set for reshuffle as S&P adopts new rules
items.excerpt: S&P Dow Jones Indices will soon change its rules for classifying growth and value shares. The new criteria will incorporate intangible assets, forward earnings, and free cash flow instead of relying on 12-month price momentum. These changes are expected to affect approximately $375 billion of passive funds linked to the index. FTSE Russell is also considering adjustments due to the dominance of technology companies.

items.title: Radhakishan Damani portfolio: Top 10 stock holdings of the ace investor
items.excerpt: Damani’s other top stock holdings in terms of holding value are United Breweries, TSF Investments, Horizon Industrial Parks, Blue Dart Express and Bhagiradha Chemicals.

items.title: BPCL reports 21.45% drop in Q2 FY27 net profit, attributes losses to fuel pricing issues
items.excerpt: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) has reported a 21.45% decline in consolidated net profit for Q2 FY27. The decline is attributed to losses from the sale of petrol, diesel, and LPG, which affected marketing margins. Consolidated revenue from operations increased by 29.7% compared to the previous fiscal year. As of September 30, 2026, BPCL's cumulative under recoveries on LPG reached ₹17,334.40 crore.

items.title: DRL says cap on trade margins a positive, posts 36% dip in Q2 PAT
items.excerpt: In the second quarter of FY2027, Dr. Reddy's Labs experienced a downturn in both revenue and profit. However, the company supports new trade margin regulations that aim to improve access to vital medicines. With a commitment to boosting its core business performance, management is also dedicated to exploring growth avenues.

items.title: Adani Power profit surges 142% on strong demand amid weak rains
items.excerpt: Adani Power has reported a 142% increase in net profit for the July-September quarter. This profit was driven by strong electricity demand and exceptional prior-period income. Operating revenue for the company saw a nearly 30% increase compared to the previous year. The company also recognized significant revenue due to adjustments in historic energy charges under its power purchase agreements.

items.title: JSW Steel posts three-fold jump in profit, lines up capacity expansion
items.excerpt: JSW Steel achieved an impressive three-fold rise in its consolidated net profit for the September quarter, highlighted by a record-breaking 13% increase in sales volumes compared to last year. The company has received approval for ambitious expansion projects, aiming to add 5 million tonnes at the Utkal site in Odisha.

items.title: 5 world market themes for the week ahead
items.excerpt: An important week is upcoming with central banks like the Federal Reserve and European Central Bank making policy decisions. Major companies, including Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft, are set to report their earnings. Political events are also significant, with elections in Israel and Brazil influencing markets. China's leadership will hold discussions focused on party governance amidst external pressures.

items.title: US consumer sentiment near record low ahead of midterm elections
items.excerpt: In October, consumer sentiment in the U.S. plummeted to a concerning 48.0, driven by rising prices and economic worries amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Survey results suggest that independents show the steepest drop in confidence, approaching historical lows. Additionally, inflation expectations have risen, marking a continuation of trends from earlier this year. Federal Reserve officials are attentively observing these shifts as they plan future interest rate adjustments.

items.title: Wall Street Week Ahead: Earnings flood, Fed meeting will test rickety AI market rally
items.excerpt: US stock investors are on the edge of their seats as they anticipate quarterly earnings from tech giants like Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon. This week is pivotal, with the Federal Reserve meeting also in sight, likely to shape how investors feel about the AI sector. After disappointing earnings from firms such as Meta and Lam Research, mixed sentiment looms over the market, especially with the midterm elections on the horizon.

items.title: Indians remit $2.7 billion overseas in August, led by travel
items.excerpt: Outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) stood at $2.7 billion, with travel accounting for the largest chunk. Indians spent $1.6 billion on travel in August, from $1.7 billion in July, while $275 million were spent on maintenan-ce of relatives. Indian citizen spent $321 million on investments in equity and debt, while $191 million on studies abroad.

items.title: Gross FDI inflows to India fall to $11 billion in August
items.excerpt: Gross foreign direct investment (FDI) to India decreased to $11 billion in August, from $14 billion a month ago. Net FDI to India slows $3 billion in August, from $7 billion in July. Financial services, communication services, computer services and manufacturing accounted for around 73% of total FDI equity inflows during April-August 2026.

items.title: Swiggy sinks 16% to record low as quick-commerce losses widen
items.excerpt: Shares of Swiggy fell by 16.4% to ₹176.70, marking a record low for the company. This decline raises concerns over cash burn and achieving profitability in its quick-commerce business. Analysts are questioning Swiggy's strategic choices and execution following its market debut. The widening losses in the quick-commerce segment have drawn attention to the company's overall performance.

items.title: BSE begins hunt for MD & CEO successor ahead of 2027 exit
items.excerpt: BSE has initiated the search for its next managing director and chief executive officer. Sundararaman Ramamurthy is scheduled to retire in June 2027 after reaching the age limit. The exchange is looking for candidates with at least 20 years of experience, which includes senior leadership roles. Applicants need to be under 62 years old as of July 1, 2027.

items.title: IndusInd Bank posts Rs 1,242 crore net profit on lower provisions
items.excerpt: IndusInd Bank reported an impressive consolidated net profit of ₹1,242 crore for the September quarter, marking a robust recovery from the previous year's loss of ₹437 crore. This turnaround stems from decreased provisions and heightened fee income, alongside encouraging trends in asset quality, evidenced by reduced non-performing asset ratios. The bank's financial outlook showcases a significant improvement in both growth and profitability.

items.title: Infosys upbeat on deals, cautious on growth as competition intensifies
items.excerpt: Infosys released its quarterly results, showing good revenue growth and stable operating margins. However, the management reduced the annual revenue guidance due to competitive pressures. The company secured a significant $2 billion deal, boosting its total contract value to $5.2 billion. Despite positive performance from some sectors, weaknesses in others contributed to the cautious outlook. The market response led to a rise in the stock price, affecting valuation metrics.

items.title: Friday blockbuster for Jio IPO: Rs 7.4 lakh crore bids, 22x subscription
items.excerpt: Jio Platforms has experienced a surge in demand for its initial public offering, garnering roughly ₹7.41 lakh crore in bids. The subscription soared to 22.19 times, mainly due to robust involvement from institutional investors, including domestic mutual funds and foreign entities. This enthusiasm contrasts with current trends in the secondary market, and shares are scheduled for listing on October 28, showcasing Jio's strides in the digital and telecommunications arenas.

items.title: Small and midcap indices post worst weekly decline in two years
items.excerpt: Mid-cap and small-cap stocks in India have faced major declines, indicating a shift in market sentiment. The Nifty MidCap 150 and Small-cap 250 indices reported their worst weekly falls in two years. Domestic retail investors initially supported these segments by increasing mutual fund contributions. However, concerns over rising oil prices and fiscal deficits are adding to market uncertainties.

items.title: RBI’s forward dollar sales surge to record $200 billion in August
items.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India recorded a net purchase of $43.26 billion in August's foreign exchange market. This was done to manage significant dollar inflows from the FCNR(B) scheme and overseas borrowings. Despite the net purchase, foreign exchange reserves did not increase due to large forex sell/buy swaps. By August 31, measures attracted over $127 billion, aiding the RBI's operations.

items.title: iPhone Duo internal display break: Are iPhone Duo displays too fragile? Users report alarming cracks near hinge
items.excerpt: Users have begun reporting instances of broken inner displays in the new iPhone Duo model. Cracks are appearing near the hinge, causing concern about the device's durability. Some owners experienced damage after minimal use, with one individual reporting a crack after just six hours. Apple is currently analyzing reported cases to determine whether there is a manufacturing issue involved.

items.title: US Markets Today: Dow ends 600 pts lower as AI doubts persist ahead of Fed meet
items.excerpt: US stocks ended lower after a turbulent week as fresh doubts over the AI trade weighed on sentiment. The Dow fell 1.25%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq also declined. Investors turned their focus to major earnings from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, along with next week’s Federal Reserve meeting.

items.title: Tata Motors CV posts Rs 2,138 crore Q2 profit
items.excerpt: Tata Motors Ltd achieved a standalone net profit of ₹2,138 crore for the September quarter, reversing last year's loss. Revenue from operations rose significantly to ₹23,930 crore, up 42% from the previous year. Improved demand was driven by higher fleet utilization and industrial activity, according to managing director Girish Wagh. Consolidated profit also increased to ₹1,257 crore, aided by a drop in mark-to-market losses.

items.title: Private sector activity hits four month high in October
items.excerpt: India's private sector activity experienced significant growth in October, reaching a four-month high as new orders increased. The HSBC Flash India Composite Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 56.7, signaling expansion. Manufacturing output and new orders remained stable, while services activity saw notable improvement. Employment increased slightly, although firms showed caution in hiring due to adequate staffing levels. International demand contributed to growth, with export orders expanding significantly during this period.

items.title: Target reached, but asset monetisation to continue: DIPAM secretary Arunish Chawla
items.excerpt: "We have already identified a cluster of 10 national highways, which will provide the underlying capital asset. So, the second public InvITs is in the works and hopefully before the close of this financial year, it will also come to fruition," Chawla said. "We are also bringing down the equity (stake) in nationalised banks gradually to the minimum public shareholding norm of 75%, that is part of the mandate that we have to share the wealth with the people and also in line with regulations...we are moving ahead on that path."

items.title: US data centre spending seen more than doubling to $2.1 trillion by 2028, estimates BoFA
items.excerpt: Global data centre spending is expected to reach $1 trillion in 2026 and more than double to $2.1 trillion by 2028, driven by rising demand for AI services, BofA Global Research estimates. The data centre market could reach $2.93 trillion by 2030 as AI fuels rapid infrastructure expansion.

items.title: Silver hits 11-month low of ₹1.95 lakh as crude stokes inflation fears

Prices have plunged ₹32,955, or more than 14%, over the past 10 sessions. A recent appreciation in the rupee has provided only limited relief against the decline in international prices.

items.title: US Treasury yields rise but 10-year stays below 5% as AI jitters persist
items.excerpt: US Treasury yields rise after a sharp drop in the previous session, but the benchmark 10 year yield stays below 5% as lingering AI market concerns keep investors cautious. Strong economic activity and sticky inflation remain key factors for bond markets, while expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike next week weaken further.

items.title: EAAA India Alternatives mops up Rs 360 crore from anchor investors; IPO opens on Oct 26

The company will not receive any proceeds from the issue as it is an offer for sale. Prominent institutional investors and major domestic mutual fund houses participated in the anchor allocation.

items.title: Shriram Finance Q2 profit jumps 59% YoY to Rs 3,677 crore on strong interest income, lower funding costs
items.excerpt: Shriram Finance reported a 59.4% year-on-year rise in Q2 FY27 standalone profit to Rs 3,677 crore, driven by higher net interest income and lower funding costs. Assets under management grew 17%, while the board declared an interim dividend of Rs 6.50 per share.

items.title: Shree Cement profit falls 15% YoY to Rs 263 crore on higher fuel costs

items.title: Jana Small Finance Bank Q2 profit jumps 127%, raises FY27 growth outlook
items.excerpt: Jana Small Finance Bank reported a 127% year-on-year rise in Q2 profit to Rs 170 crore, supported by business growth, higher margins and improved gross asset quality. The bank raised its annual profit growth guidance to 100%, while loans and deposits expanded.

items.title: RBI flags rising inflation risks from West Asia conflict, El Nino despite resilient Indian economy
items.excerpt: India's external sector shows resilience due to a narrowing trade gap and comfortable foreign exchange reserves. Inflationary pressures have intensified due to geopolitical tensions and supply-side bottlenecks. The RBI reported an increase in both industry and services indicators, showcasing economic strength. The IMF has revised India's growth projection for 2026-27 to 7% based on resilient domestic demand. Global financial volatility has increased amid global challenges and rising inflation risks.

items.title: Jindal Steel Q2 profit rises 21% as revenue hits record Rs 19,448 crore
items.excerpt: Jindal Steel’s Q2 FY26 profit rose 21% year-on-year to Rs 771 crore, while revenue surged 44% to a record Rs 19,448 crore. Higher steel production and sales boosted earnings, while adjusted EBITDA grew 33% and net debt declined sequentially.

items.title: BPCL Q2 Results: Net profit declines 21% YoY to Rs 4,863 crore, revenue grows 29%
items.excerpt: BPCL reported a 21.45% year-on-year decline in Q2 FY27 profit to Rs 4,863.05 crore, despite 29.78% revenue growth. Sequential performance rebounded sharply from a quarterly loss, while the company approved a subsidiary for its proposed Andhra Pradesh refinery.

items.excerpt: Aditya Birla Real Estate Ltd has announced plans to develop a housing project in Pune. This initiative will generate an estimated revenue of Rs 1,650 crore through a Joint Development Agreement. Birla Estates, a subsidiary of Aditya Birla Real Estate, will oversee the project development.

items.title: A hidden bias in human language challenges 70 years of science
items.excerpt: A groundbreaking study challenges 70 years of assumptions about how human language works. By analyzing billions of word uses, scientists discovered that meaning is organized around power, danger, and order rather than emotion alone. Even more surprisingly, human language shows a powerful hidden preference for safety, suggesting that our words may reflect ancient survival instincts.

items.title: NASA’s asteroid Bennu samples reveal a 4.5-billion-year-old secret
items.excerpt: Tiny samples from asteroid Bennu are rewriting scientists' understanding of how our Solar System formed. New evidence suggests that Bennu was born where material from the inner and outer Solar System mixed, with Jupiter playing a surprising role in shaping its formation.

items.title: Could lowering high blood pressure be as simple as stimulating your ear?
items.excerpt: A small device that gently stimulates nerves through the ear could offer a new way to tackle stubborn high blood pressure. In a clinical trial of 63 patients already taking medication, the treatment proved safe, easy to use at home, and well tolerated. Although it did not significantly outperform a placebo overall, patients with more severe hypertension showed promising reductions in blood pressure.

items.title: Scientists propose a way to detect dangerous “mirror life” before it exists
items.excerpt: Scientists have proposed a way to detect “mirror life,” a hypothetical form of life that could pose serious risks to humans, animals, and ecosystems if artificially created. Using special fluorescent molecules and a type of polarized light also used in 3D movie technology, researchers believe they could distinguish ordinary organisms from their mirror-image counterparts.

items.title: Astronomers uncover a mysterious magnetic web above the Sun
items.excerpt: The Sun’s seemingly peaceful regions are hiding a surprisingly complex magnetic world. Using a balloon-borne telescope high above Earth, scientists discovered delicate, thread-like magnetic structures woven through the solar atmosphere, apparently shaped by twisting motions on the Sun’s surface. They also mapped magnetic fields inside towering jets of solar material, revealing how those fields change with height.

items.title: These tiny snakes roll four times faster than they slither
items.excerpt: Tiny snakes in Southeast Asia have mastered an extraordinary escape technique: rolling across the ground at speeds up to four times faster than ordinary slithering. Scientists discovered that dwarf reedsnakes accomplish this feat through precisely coordinated body movements that allow their bodies to rotate while their heads remain remarkably stable.

items.title: This 150-million-year-old bird had dinosaur teeth and a strange secret
items.excerpt: A 150-million-year-old fossil discovered in China reveals a bizarre early bird with sharp teeth, a dinosaur-like claw, and a body built for life on the ground rather than flight. Scientists believe it represents the earliest known example of flight loss in birds, overturning assumptions about how these animals evolved.

items.title: One of Earth’s most powerful supervolcanoes is refilling with fresh magma
items.excerpt: Deep beneath Japan’s Kikai caldera, a massive magma reservoir is refilling 7,300 years after one of the most powerful volcanic eruptions in Earth's recent geological history. Scientists used underwater seismic surveys to reveal a vast store of magma that appears to have accumulated since the ancient catastrophe. The discovery could help explain how supervolcanoes like Yellowstone and Toba rebuild their magma supplies.

items.title: Scientists discover a hidden switch that burns fat and blocks new fat cells
items.excerpt: Scientists have discovered that switching off a protein called Mitch makes human cells burn more fat and prevents new fat cells from developing. The breakthrough builds on experiments in mice that showed remarkable resistance to obesity and improved muscular endurance, raising hopes for a new approach to weight-loss treatment.

items.title: Dental implants can hijack your immune system, scientists discover
items.excerpt: Researchers have uncovered a surprising reason dental implant infections often resist antibiotics: the implants themselves can contribute to the problem. Bacteria corrode titanium implants, releasing microscopic particles that hijack immune cells, trigger destructive inflammation, and accelerate jawbone loss.

items.title: Breakthrough PTSD treatment achieves 68% remission rate in clinical trial
items.excerpt: A newly FDA-cleared PTSD treatment uses personalized brain mapping and magnetic stimulation to target abnormal brain activity, with a clinical trial reporting a 52% reduction in symptoms and 68% remission. Researchers believe the technology could transform PTSD care and pave the way for more precise treatments for other mental health conditions.

items.title: Scientists discover a surprising double benefit of exercise for Parkinson’s
items.excerpt: A seven-year study found that people with Parkinson’s disease who were more physically active experienced slower declines in memory, thinking, and movement abilities. Those exercising more than eight hours per week showed almost no average cognitive decline, suggesting that staying active may offer important benefits as the disease progresses.

items.title: Scientists discover a hidden messaging system deep inside the brain
items.excerpt: A tiny region deep within the brain has surprised scientists by revealing a remarkably sophisticated communication system. Previously thought to broadcast the same chemical signal throughout the brain, this region actually sends targeted messages that help control learning, attention, and behavior, according to new research in mice.

items.title: Glioblastoma breakthrough reveals how brain cancer cells become more aggressive
items.excerpt: Scientists discovered that the thick, sticky fluid surrounding glioblastoma tumors can make brain cancer cells smaller, more flexible, and better at invading surrounding tissue. Even more troubling, some of these changes persist after the cells leave the thick fluid, revealing a previously overlooked mechanism that could help this deadly cancer spread.

items.title: Elusive uranium 'sandwich' molecule isolated after more than 50 years
items.excerpt: Elusive uranium 'sandwich' molecule isolated after more than 50 years October 23, 2026 Elusive uranium 'sandwich' molecule isolated after more than 50 years by Conrad Goodwin, University of Manchester edited by Lisa Lock, reviewed by Robert Egan Credit: University of Manchester In a study published in Nature Communications, researchers from The University of Manchester and Lancaster University have isolated and characterized uranocenium, the positively charged form of a landmark uranium compound called uranocene. The work shows that this long-sought molecule is stable, and that it behaves in a way that challenges how chemists usually think about bonding in heavy elements. Uranocene is a 'sandwich' molecule: a single uranium atom held between two flat rings, each made of eight carbon atoms. It is the uranium counterpart of ferrocene, an iron sandwich molecule whose discovery contributed to the 1973 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Ferrocene readily gives up an electron to form the ferrocenium cation, a switch so clean and reliable that it is used as a reference standard in laboratories worldwide. Until now, no one had been able to isolate the equivalent uranium compound. They used single-crystal X-ray diffraction, which maps the positions of atoms in a crystal, alongside magnetic and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) measurements, which probe the unpaired electrons inside a molecule, and computer modeling. Together, these confirmed that the uranium has given up one more electron than in uranocene, raising its "oxidation state" from +4 to +5. Electrochemical experiments, which measure how easily a molecule gains or loses electrons, showed that uranocene and uranocenium switch back and forth as cleanly as ferrocene and ferrocenium do. This signaled to the researchers that the molecular structure barely changes when the electron is added or removed. Publication details Cameron N. items.excerpt: ALMA spots 'dragon egg' that may represent the earliest stages of massive star formation October 23, 2026 report ALMA spots 'dragon egg' that may represent the earliest stages of massive star formation by Shreejaya Karantha, Phys.org edited by Lisa Lock, reviewed by Robert Egan ALMA 1 mm continuum emission toward the C2c1 region. Credit: arXiv (2026). DOI: 10.48550/arxiv.2610.07138 Astronomers identified an exceptionally tiny core that may represent an early stage in the formation of a massive star. Located in an infrared-dark area called Dragon Cloud, the core is nicknamed the "dragon egg." The paper, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics, was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 5. Astronomers observed one such promising candidate called C2c1a in the C2c1 region inside an infrared-dark cloud known as Dragon Cloud, located about 16,300 light-years away. Nicknamed the "dragon egg," the core appears to contain some 20 to 30 times the sun's mass. The clump around it holds roughly 1,061 times the mass of the sun but gives off little energy for its size. This, researchers say, is a sign of a "very early stage of high-mass star formation." Earlier data could not confirm whether C2c1a is one compact object, where its mass is concentrated, or whether a protostar has formed. High-resolution data revealed that the main region itself has six components: C2c1a(a), C2c1b, and four fainter structures in the intervening envelope. The emission was dominated by the central component C2c1a(a). This indicates that most of the emission comes from a centrally concentrated region. The core is embedded in a much larger reservoir of cold gas and dust with a mass of at least around 110 times the sun's mass. This could supply the material needed to form a massive star. A. T. Despite the scale of the outbreak, no vaccine has yet been approved specifically against the Bundibugyo virus. Tumaini, meaning "hope" in Swahili, aims to assess the safety, immune responses and effectiveness of several vaccine candidates, particularly among people who have been in contact with confirmed Ebola patients and face a high risk of infection. The trial uses an adaptive platform design, allowing multiple vaccine candidates to be evaluated within a single study through a ring vaccination approach targeting contacts of confirmed cases. The first vaccine entering the trial is Ervebo, which is already licensed to prevent disease caused by the Zaire Ebola virus but has not been proven effective against the Bundibugyo virus.
